name: Malta
summary: Children are guaranteed a third of the estate (a half with five or more children). A foreign resident can choose the law of their nationality (EU Succession Regulation art. 22). Malta has its own trust law, has been a Hague Trusts Convention state since 1996, and allows private foundations.
reserved_share: Descendants: legitim of 1/3 of the estate if there are up to four children, 1/2 if five or more, shared among all children (Civil Code art. 616). The surviving spouse and ascendants have further protections whose figures were not sourced.
foreign_law_note: EU Succession Regulation: the law of the last habitual residence applies by default (art. 21), but a resident foreign national may choose the law of their nationality (art. 22).
trust_note: The 1985 Hague Trusts Convention entered into force for Malta on 1 March 1996 (accession 7 December 1994). Trusts are governed by the Trusts and Trustees Act (Cap. 331), and private foundations by the Civil Code (Second Schedule, Foundations). Both are taken from general knowledge, not checked in this pass.
open_questions: The e-Justice Malta page could not be fetched; art. 616 comes from a search summary of the e-Justice factsheet.
The surviving spouse's and ascendants' reserved rights (e.g. right of habitation, Civil Code arts. 615 and 631) were not sourced.
